notes:
Top-line: Suncrest is a B2B SaaS (support automation) with ~450 engineers and an aggressive roadmap to ship AI-first features. They evaluated Redwood Hosted API first (fast onboarding) and are now moving to a Dedicated POC to validate production economics and reliability. Key PV: low p95 latency for chat (target <= 180ms per token on short-turn interactions), steady throughput for peak support hours (~120 concurrent chat sessions), and clear rollback/fallback behavior.

POC ask (high level):
- Dedicated pool with 4 gpus (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), ability to scale to 8 during peaks.
- Canary routing: route 5% of prod traffic to Redwood Dedicated model variant (quantized Q4-8) for 48 hours, monitor latency, token cost, and response quality (BLEU-like heuristics + human eval).
- Fallback plan: automatic region failover to hosted API in the event of Dedicated capacity degradation; model variant fallback from LLaMA-2-70B-qat to LLaMA-2-13B-q4 if latency > 300ms p95 or error rate > 2%.
- Rollback: immediate traffic cutover to previous model + traffic to fallback region with health check gating.

Security/Compliance notes: CISO requires SAML integration and audit logging for token-level requests. Data residency preference: US-east primary, EU for EU customers. Legal flagged retention controls for transcripts (retain 30 days by default, archive for 12 months for escalations).

Commercial: Their procurement team asked for a 6-month reserved estimate and a PO route if POC succeeds. Finance sensitivity: want host/dedicated cost breakdown (per-token + infra amortized) and clear throttles.

Quote from PM Elena on 2026-01-18 call: "We need predictable latency — if the model slows under load we lose trust quickly. Canary needs to be surgical and reversible."

References: Fireflies ff-2026-01-18-76431; security FAQ in Drive. Jira RW-3421 is for KMS integration questions.

AE notes (Jordan): keep POC tight (2 weeks), require templated canary runbook + rollback playbook from Redwood SEs before start.
requirements_summary: Workload: customer support chat + doc search + reranking. Latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms (short prompts) and p95 <= 350ms (longer). Throughput target: ~120 concurrent sessions with average 30 tokens/session/turn. Model preferences: high-quality open models with quantized variants; require deterministic fallback mapping (70B -> 13B). Routing needs: per-route canary, region failover, automatic rollback. Security: SAML SSO, SOC2, KMS encryption, audit logs, data residency controls.
poc_plan: Prep week: exchange network/VPC details, KMS test keys, create service accounts.
Day 1: Provision Dedicated pool (4 GPUs) in us-east, deploy primary model variant and 13B fallback variant.
Day 2: Sanity tests (latency, cold start, KV caching) with synthetic workload.
Day 3–4: Canary ramp to 5% production traffic; run quality checks (automated metrics + 10 human evals/day).
Day 5: Run region failover test: force a simulated Dedicated region outage and validate auto-failover to hosted API (metrics, logs).
Day 6–10: Increase canary to 15% if p95 and error rates within thresholds, run cost telemetry checks.
End of week 2: Final evaluation meeting; decision: proceed to reserved commit or rollback to hosted-only.
acceptance_criteria: Latency: Dedicated p95 <= 180ms for short-turn chat in canary at 5% load.
Reliability: Error rate < 1% during POC and successful automatic failover test.
Quality: Human evals show parity or acceptable delta vs current in-house model on top-10 intents.
Cost: Estimated per-token + infra cost results in <= 30% overall cost increase vs hosted with better latency (finance threshold).
Operational: Runbook for canary + rollback accepted by Suncrest infra team.
